title: Divine Ethics · 99-item compilation · relevant selection
note: Selected foundational, individual-ethics, learning and ethical-conduct questions from the 99-item compilation. Not a complete authenticated exam sitting. Medical rulings, marriage questions, unclear items and redundant copies are excluded. Several printed keys are corrected; all answers are editorially checked and retain the original key in the explanation/download. No official I/II label is claimed.
courseEvidence: Admitted by question-level comparison with the supplied review and first-term lessons, as requested. The original lacks a confirmed university I/II course code; content match is not a claim of official enrollment or syllabus completeness.
dateEvidence: Sitting date not established; no date is inferred from a download or Telegram posting.

audit.method: Source wording and option order checked against original pages/native text; answers compared with the current review, first-term notes and specified primary passages. Content relevance is not official course-code authentication. No official key is asserted.

questions.prompt: According to Islam, where does healing come from?
options: From God; medicine, drugs and other things are just tools.
questions.topic: Trust in God and responsible effort
questions.note: The review p. 8 describes medicine as a dependent cause in its theological account. This does not replace medical treatment; use of effective means is explicitly required.
questions.reviewNote: Dependent means and the example of medicine, review p. 8.

questions.prompt: Why is human nature unable to distinguish between what is good and what is wrong?
options: Because he wants to make a mistake.
Because he did not know what was good in his life.
Because he thinks what he is doing is good.
Because man polluted his nature with national sins and prejudices.
questions.note: The question overgeneralizes: the course is explaining obscured discernment, not a universal inability. Lesson 3, p. 7 attributes this to corruption of the original disposition and obstructing desires, making D the best supplied choice. The source’s phrase “national sins” is retained as a translation defect. The printed key C does not identify the taught cause.

questions.note: A is the only comprehensive option. First-term Lesson 2 includes both good and bad traits and actions. Neither right-only nor wrong-only describes the full field.

questions.prompt: The three major areas of study within ethics recognized today are:
options: Social ethics, normative ethics and behavioral ethics.

Behavioral ethics, normative ethics and medical ethics.
questions.note: B is the standard three-area classification used by this compilation. First-term pp. 4–5 explain meta-ethics, prescriptive/command discussion and applied ethics; they also discuss descriptive ethics separately.
